# clusterComposer

`clusterComposer` generates bespoke spatial sampling frames from
building footprints or building locations. It groups buildings into spatially
defined sampling units for use in survey design or updating census frames.

## Installation

### Linux system dependencies

On Ubuntu or Debian, install the required system libraries before installing
`clusterComposer`:

```{bash, eval=FALSE}
sudo apt update
sudo apt install libgdal-dev libgeos-dev libproj-dev libglpk-dev
```

You can install the development version of `clusterComposer` like so:

``` r
# if the pak package is not installed, install this first:
install.packages("pak")

# use the following two lines to install clusterComposer with vignettes available
Sys.setenv(PKG_BUILD_VIGNETTES = "true")
pak::pak("cadooley/clusterComposer",dependencies = TRUE)

# once installed, load the clusterComposer package 
library(clusterComposer)

# if helpful, explore vignettes for a full walk through of downloading and preparing data followed by running the cluster composer function to create a sampling frame
vignette("clusterComposer", package = "clusterComposer")

```

## Citation

If you use `clusterComposer`, please cite the
package:

Dooley, C. A., Clary, C. B., Rhoda, D. A., & Thomson, D. R. (2026). *clusterComposer: Generate Bespoke Spatial Sampling Frames from Buildings.* R package version 0.1.1. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24353237. Repository: https://github.com/cadooley/clusterComposer.

## User instructions

`clusterComposer` generates clusters that meet a target population size with well defined polygon boundaries. `clusterComposer` requires two input datasets: 1. area of interest cut up into sections. Each section must have a clean single polygon geometry. The area of interest can be read into R from any suitable spatial file and could be cleaned in R prior to running `clusterComposer`; 2: building footprints, each with an associated population count. If building footprints are not available, the geometries could be buffered point locations converted into polygons. The building footprints file must be in geopackage format. 

Users must specify the name of the aoi sf object (`aoi`), the file path for the building footprints geopackage (`bf_file_path`), a run ID that forms the name of the output file (`run_id`), and the file path for the output file (`output_file_path`). It is recommended that users specify a suitable number of cores (`n_cores`) as the function splits processing across available computing cores to reduce running time. If needed, the target population per cluster (`pop_per_EZ`) can be specified. The default is 250 people per cluster. Note that if this is changed, users should also change the minimum (`min_pop_per_EZ`) and maximum (`max_pop_per_EZ`) population per cluster values too.

  
While `clusterComposer` is under development, we recommend that `delete_temp_files` is set to `FALSE`. If set to `TRUE`, intermediate files are deleted when the function exits. Setting to `FALSE` means that results for completed sections can be used/reviewed if an error occurs. These can be found in the "temporary" folder inside the `output_file_path` directory.

Example running code:


```{r example, eval=FALSE}

library(clusterComposer)

# read in Area of Interest (aoi)
AOI <- sf::st_read("cities_data/kolkata_sections.gpkg") 
# define number of computing cores
ncores <- parallel::detectCores() - 1

# run clusterComposer function
clusterComposer(aoi=AOI,
                bf_file_path = "cities_data/buildingsWithPop_kolkata.gpkg",
                run_id = "kolkata_20261117",
                output_file_path = "cities_output",
                pop_per_EZ=250,
                max_pop_per_EZ=350,
                min_pop_per_EZ=150,
                n_cores = ncores,
                delete_temp_files = FALSE
)
```

## Method overview

The clusterComposer function performs the steps outlined below. Here is an example set of building footprints obtained from the Overture Maps
Foundation buildings dataset (Overture Maps Foundation, accessed November 2026).

![Example building footprints from Kolkata, India. Data attribution: Overture Maps Foundation, overturemaps.org. © OpenStreetMap
contributors.*](man/figures/Kolkata_section46_bfs.png)

&nbsp;

**STEP 1:** buffer buildings and merge areas of overlap to create collections of buildings in close proximity. Buffer distance is set such that a collection does not exceed the max population per cluster (enumeration zone) and therefore each collection may have a different buffer distance.

![Step 1: create collections of buildings in close proximity. Data attribution: Overture Maps Foundation, overturemaps.org. © OpenStreetMap
contributors.*](man/figures/Kolkata_section46_step1_buffering.png)

&nbsp;

**STEP 2:** create minimum area rectangles around building collections and merge rectangles with significant overlap to define sensible cluster areas (this prevents different collections of buildings from being too intertwined).

![Step 2: create block shapes around building collections. Data attribution: Overture Maps Foundation, overturemaps.org. © OpenStreetMap
contributors.*](man/figures/Kolkata_section46_step2_minarearect.png)

&nbsp;

**STEP 3:** apply hierarchical clustering to spatially combine blocks of building collections to meet target population per cluster.

![Step 3: apply hierarchical clustering. Data attribution: Overture Maps Foundation, overturemaps.org. © OpenStreetMap
contributors.*](man/figures/Kolkata_section46_step3_hierclust.png)

&nbsp;

**STEP 4:** allocate any small spaces between clusters to neighbouring clusters with the longest shared boundary.

![Step 4: merge small inter-cluster spaces with suitable clusters. Data attribution: Overture Maps Foundation, overturemaps.org. © OpenStreetMap
contributors.*](man/figures/Kolkata_section46_step4_spacescleanup.png)

![Post Step 4 population per cluster. Data attribution: Overture Maps Foundation, overturemaps.org. © OpenStreetMap
contributors.*](man/figures/Kolkata_section46_step5_presteppop.png)

&nbsp;

**STEP 5:** combine any clusters below minimum population per cluster to a suitable neighbouring cluster. Clusters are combined only if the resulting population does not exceed the maximum threshold. Where multiple valid combinations are possible, the combination that produces the most spatially compact cluster is performed.

![Step 5: combine any clusters below minimum population per cluster to a suitable neighbouring cluster. Data attribution: Overture Maps Foundation, overturemaps.org. © OpenStreetMap
contributors.*](man/figures/Kolkata_section46_step5_addlowpopclusts.png)

&nbsp;

**STEP 6:** clean up cluster boundaries to produce lines that go around buildings and are sensible, i.e. not wobbly.

![Step 6: clean up cluster boundaries. Data attribution: Overture Maps Foundation, overturemaps.org. © OpenStreetMap
contributors.*](man/figures/Kolkata_section46_step6_boundarycleanup.png)
